claims.text: Conventionally processed single-phase ZrB2 requires processing above 2300 °C.
Single-phase ZrB2 exhibits strong Zr–B and B–B interactions.
Lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens are vulnerable to oxidation.
Lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens are vulnerable to liquid-metal corrosion.
Adding a modest volume fraction of SiC and sintering at approximately 1700 °C will produce an in-situ intergranular silica/borosilicate phase.
SiC reacts with minor surface oxides or borides on ZrB2 during lower-temperature sintering.
The proposed reaction generates a continuous protective phase at ZrB2 grain boundaries.
The intergranular silica/borosilicate phase limits oxygen ingress by acting as a diffusion barrier.
The intergranular phase limits attack by liquid plating metal.
The intergranular phase helps maintain mechanical integrity by bonding ZrB2 grains.
The ZrB2–SiC composite will have lower oxidation weight gain than the specified controls.
The ZrB2–SiC composite will have greater resistance to liquid plating-metal corrosion than the specified controls.
The approximately 1700 °C ZrB2–SiC composite will have hardness comparable to or slightly greater than high-temperature-processed single-phase ZrB2.
The approximately 1700 °C ZrB2–SiC composite will have strength comparable to or slightly greater than high-temperature-processed single-phase ZrB2.
Prior lower-temperature specimens without SiC had poorer oxidation resistance than the proposed composite is expected to have.
Prior lower-temperature specimens without SiC had poorer liquid-metal corrosion resistance than the proposed composite is expected to have.
